    Context OS for AI Development

    Your AI sees everything.
    Make it see what matters.

    LeanCTX is the operating system for AI context. It decides what your AI sees, remembers, and focuses on — so every answer is faster, smarter, and more accurate. One binary, zero config, works with Cursor, Claude Code, Copilot, and 24+ tools.

    The Problem

    AI tools flood the model with noise.

    Every file read, every shell command, every search result — your AI sends it all to the model without filtering. The result? Slower responses, higher costs, and an AI that loses focus in its own context window.

    "The bottleneck isn't the model. It's what you feed it."

    Without lean-ctx
    AI reads 800-line file
    → Thousands of tokens sent to LLM
    Includes comments, whitespace, imports
    → Slow, expensive, hits context limits
    With lean-ctx
    AI reads 800-line file
    → lean-ctx compresses via AST parsing
    Keeps types, signatures, logic
    → 60–90% fewer tokens, same signal
    See It In Action

    What it looks like in your terminal.

    lean-ctx works silently behind the scenes. When your AI reads a file, the context layer transparently compresses, routes, and optimizes the output. Here's a real ctx_read call and the metrics dashboard.

    ctx_read — map
    AI calls: ctx_read({ path: "src/lib/mcpManifest.ts", mode: "map" })
    schema_version 1
    tools.granular 49
    tools.unified 5
    read_modes 10
    modes: auto, full, map, signatures, diff, aggressive
    What is LeanCTX?

    A runtime that makes AI agents smarter.

    Sees Smarter

    Compresses files intelligently — keeping types, signatures, and logic while removing noise. Your AI reads 10x more code in the same context window.

    Remembers Better

    Cross-session memory, knowledge graphs, and context checkpoints. Your AI knows what happened yesterday, not just what's in the current prompt.

    Works Controlled

    Profiles, roles, budgets, and SLOs. Define how much context each agent uses, what tools they can access, and when to throttle.

    Four Dimensions of Context Intelligence

    Everything between your code and the AI, handled.

    01

    Intelligent Compression

    10 read modes — from full file to entropy-filtered — let the AI choose the right compression per file. Tree-sitter AST parsing for 18 languages strips syntax noise. Cached re-reads return in ~13 tokens. Result: 60–99% fewer tokens with zero information loss.

    02

    Smart Routing

    Every request is classified by intent — What, How, or Do — to select the optimal read mode and compression level automatically. Regex search returns compact matches, not entire files. Cross-file deduplication removes shared imports and repeated patterns.

    03

    Persistent Memory

    Context checkpoints preserve session state across conversations. Knowledge graphs track file relationships, discoveries, and decisions. Multi-agent handoffs keep context intact when work is split between agents. Nothing is lost between sessions.

    04

    Output Verification

    Every compressed output is verified before delivery — path anchoring ensures file references stay valid, identifier checking catches renamed symbols, and structural integrity validates that no important context was dropped during compression.

    60–99% token reduction per file read — intent-aware compression adapts per task type, cached re-reads reach 99%
    49 context layer tools with intent-aware compression, session memory, and multi-agent support
    10 Read modes
    0 configuration required — install, init, done. Auto-adapts per client including Claude Code's 2048-char pipeline
    Architecture

    Three independent context components.

    Each component works independently. Together, they form a context pipeline that filters, compresses, prioritizes, and translates information before it reaches the LLM — turning raw data into structured intelligence.

    Context Server

    49 intelligent tools replace built-in file reads, shell commands, and code search. Understands your intent, selects the right compression mode per task type, tracks context window pressure, and manages cross-session memory — all autonomously.

    Explore tools

    Shell Hook

    Intercepts shell output and recognizes 90+ command patterns — git, npm, cargo, docker, kubectl — compressing everything automatically.

    View patterns

    Protocols

    Three protocols — CEP (efficiency scoring), CCP (cross-session memory), TDD (symbol shorthand) — teach the AI to communicate leaner. 8–25% additional token savings.

    Learn more
    The stack

    Five layers. One runtime.

    LeanCTX is not just a prompt helper. It’s an end-to-end runtime: explicit I/O tools, orchestration, memory policies, verification, and delivery artifacts you can run.

    L1 Live I/O Tools

    Controlled file reads, semantic search, and shell execution — with caching and compression modes.

    Learn more
    L2 Live Orchestration

    Intent + mode dispatch, guardrails, and tool routing so agents stay inside policy.

    Learn more
    L3 Live Memory Platform

    Policy-driven knowledge, episodic, and procedural memory — retrieval modes, feedback, and relations.

    Learn more
    L4 Live Verification

    Output verification and CI gates that catch drift, missing paths, and broken contracts early.

    Learn more
    L5 Live Delivery

    Cookbook + SDK + examples that talk to a real <code>lean-ctx serve</code> — no demos.

    Context as Code

    Configure your AI's context like infrastructure.

    Profiles define how your AI reads, compresses, and remembers. Version-control your context strategy. Share configurations across teams.

    Learn about Profiles
    .lean-ctx/profiles/review.toml
    [profile]
name = "review"
description = "Code review with broad context"

[read]
default_mode = "map"
max_tokens_per_file = 80000

[budget]
max_context_tokens = 150000
max_cost_usd = 2.0

[verification]
strict_mode = true
